---
title: "Quiz · Understand a Pico"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you can
self-grade after answering.

## 1. In one sentence, what is a Pico?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
A minimal core that composes explicit capabilities, not an application
that must pull in a framework stack. See the
[lesson](index.qmd#what-a-pico-is-and-is-not).
:::

## 2. Match each term to its one-sentence meaning.

a. **capability** — ?
b. **capsule definition** — ?
c. **capsule implementation** — ?
d. **composed Pico** — ?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
- **capability**: a named, provider-neutral action or function a Pico
  may need (e.g. `greeting`, `email.send`).
- **capsule definition**: a declarative contract describing one
  capability (identity, version, inputs, outputs, dependencies). The
  shape is the memo26 proposal and is not yet adopted upstream.
- **capsule implementation**: the concrete code that satisfies a
  capsule definition behind its contract, keeping third-party
  dependencies local.
- **composed Pico**: a Pico built by selecting a minimal core and
  binding the capsule capabilities it needs, rather than hard-wiring a
  framework stack.
:::

## 3. Which fields does `definitions/pico.yaml` require on an OE-shaped Pico, and does it name Face, Memory, or Nervous System as required?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Required fields: `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata.name`, and
`spec.{type, capabilities, implementation, state, events}`.

No anatomy item (Face, Muscles, Memory, Hands, Nervous System, Rules,
Discovery, Operations) is named as a required field. They are
capabilities a Pico composes when its purpose requires them; the
schema requires none of them by name.
:::

## 4. When this course says "Composer", does it mean capability composition?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
No. In this repository, "Composer" refers to `pico compose`, which
turns a parsed Rule into an executable shell-script artefact
(`bin/pico` lines 56 and 82–86, verified in memo24 §2.4). It currently
handles only `kind: greeting`. It is **not** a capability composer: it
does not resolve capsule dependencies, bind interfaces, or check
compatibility across capsule contracts. Capability composition is a
separate, upstream-owned concern (memo26 §4 open question 4).
:::

## 5. Where does the capsule contract live, and does this course ask you to author a capsule file?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The capsule contract would live upstream in
`open-engineering-capsules/source`. As of 2026-10-16 that repository
contains only `README.md` and a generated-placeholder `metadata.yaml`
(`lifecycle: proposed`) — no schema, no example, no composition rule
(memo24 §2.1). The capsule shape shown in the lesson is the memo26
proposal and is explicitly labelled as not yet adopted upstream. This
course does **not** ask you to author or validate a capsule file.
:::

## 6. Why is coupling a Pico's core directly to a database, broker, or AI library costly?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Because every test, every environment, and every learner inherits the
install, runtime, and version-skew burden of each dependency even when
the capability under test does not need it. Keeping capabilities
behind capsule contracts keeps implementation-specific dependencies
local to the capability that uses them, so the core and every other
capability remain testable in isolation. This is the motivation behind
memo23 §5 rules 1–3 (minimal core, optional by default, explicit
dependencies).
:::
